correctness.rationale: Let M=J²=V⊗V. For any proper two-sided ideal I⊂J, its projection U⊂V and intersection W=I∩M necessarily obey V⊗U+U⊗V⊂W. The quotient M/(V⊗U+U⊗V) is (V/U)⊗², so choosing W amounts to a w-plane B there and choosing I amounts to an arbitrary linear graph map U→(V/U)⊗²/B. Conversely each triple defines an ideal (J³=0). The dimension formula and Grassmannian/vector-bundle ranks give the Gaussian-binomial finite-field polynomial for all n≥1, all prime-power q, with whole A included separately. For n=2 and dim I=4, only U=0,W=M (vertex) or dim U=1,B=0 occur. The Plücker coordinates [Z:a³:a²b:ab²:b³] yield the reduced twisted-cubic projective cone, with singular vertex J² and q²+q+1 rational points. Independent arithmetic q=2,3,5,7 returns respectively 7,13,31,57 such ideals; source exhaustive closure checks n=1 q=2/3/5 and n=2 q=2/3. Nonreduced ideal scheme structure and all components for arbitrary n are expressly excluded.
